title: Think Outside the Data: Colonial Biases and Systemic Issues in Automated Moderation Pipelines for Low-Resource Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with AI experts, evaluating how English-centric NLP preprocessing techniques (e.g., tokenization, stemming) and multilingual models structurally fail on morphologically complex, agglutinative, and code-mixed low-resource languages.

Analysis of expert interviews highlighting how Western-centric sentiment and toxicity analysis tools misinterpret local socio-cultural contexts, dialects, and slang in the Global South, often misclassifying benign local expressions as harmful.

Applying a decolonial theoretical lens to interview data to examine structural inequities in moderation pipelines, such as the reliance on colonial-era texts (e.g., outdated Bible translations) for training data and the imposition of Euro-modern normative values on diverse populations.
